# What the model sees from ko's pi extension

Generated by scripts/dump-prompts.ts from share/pi/ko-pi.ts. Edit the source, not this file.

## Guidelines added to the system prompt (before_agent_start)

```
Never run `sleep` in bash to wait for anything - an async job, a subagent, a message, or another agent's work settling. What you are waiting for arrives as a notice or message that wakes you after you end your turn; if a build breaks because of another agent's half-done work, report that rather than sleeping until it clears. Ending your turn while you wait is always safe: a running async job or subagent of yours keeps you alive, and its notice starts your next turn.

The user runs the ko terminal multiplexer, and this pi runs in one of its panes. When the user talks about windows, tabs, panes, sessions, splits, floats or the sidebar, read the ko skill first.

While a non-service async job of yours is running, or a subagent of yours still owes you a report, ending your turn sends nothing to your parent. You were spawned as a subagent: your report is the last message of a turn that ends after all of them finish, once for each piece of work your parent gives you. Your parent is not watching this session and reads nothing else. End your work with a message that stands on its own: what you did, what failed, and what you left undone. If you must stop to wait for another agent or for the user, say so in that message; when the work completes later, tell your parent with message_agent. Reporting does not end this session: it stays alive until your parent ends it with stop_agent, and the parent can continue it with message_agent.
```

## Tools

### list_agents

description:

```
List the agents you can message: your subagents, your peers, each ancestor and its peers, in this session. which selects all (default), peers or subagents. An own subagent's row says whether it has reported on its last work and starts its last report; read_report gives the whole text. Bash jobs are in list_async_bash.
```

promptSnippet:

```
list_agents(which?) - discover the agents you can message, and your own subagents to stop with stop_agent
```

parameters:

- `which` (string | string | string): all (default), peers, or subagents (your own).

### read_report

description:

```
The whole last report of one of your subagents, or all of its reports in order, as they reached you.
```

promptSnippet:

```
read_report(agent, which?) - the whole report of one of your subagents
```

parameters:

- `agent` (string, required): A subagent of yours: its exact name, session id, a unique id prefix of at least eight characters, or an @-mention.
- `which` (string | string): last (default) or all of its reports, in order.

### list_async_bash

description:

```
List your own async_bash jobs: all running, all with an undelivered ending notice, and the newest 20 announced endings, newest first, with the job id that stop_async_bash takes and the log that holds the output.
```

promptSnippet:

```
list_async_bash() - your own async_bash jobs, with their output logs
```

parameters: none

### message_agent

description:

```
Send text to an agent by name, session id, or unique id prefix. message (default) queues for any agent until its current turn ends; to an ended subagent of yours it resumes that subagent in its own session, with its history, and the message is its next turn. steer joins the current turn of any agent in your scope. interrupt-and-steer aborts the current turn of any agent in your scope, then starts a new turn with the text.
```

promptSnippet:

```
message_agent(to, message, mode?) - send a message to another agent in this session
```

parameters:

- `to` (string, required): Who to message: an agent's exact name, session id, a unique id prefix of at least 8 characters, or an @-mention from the prompt such as @impl (session 9702ddd1).
- `message` (string, required): The message text to deliver.
- `mode` (string | string | string): message queues until the turn ends, and resumes an ended subagent of yours with its history (default). steer joins the current turn of any agent in your scope. interrupt-and-steer aborts its current turn, then starts a new turn with the text.

### spawn_agent

description:

```
Start an agent in a new window. Resume a saved session or fork a copy of it; fork alone copies this session. Returns the pi session id for later resume_from. Children report by notice and stay alive. A toplevel agent is an independent peer: no report, notice, depth limit or descendant controls; fork is allowed, but an existing child cannot become a peer.
```

promptSnippet:

```
spawn_agent(task, name, model?, cwd?, resume_from?, fork?, toplevel?, runtime?) - start, resume or copy an agent in a new window; returns its pi session id; toplevel starts an independent peer, not a child; runtime works in a configured runtime or an ad-hoc runtime of this session
```

promptGuidelines (merged into the system prompt's rules while the tool is registered):

```
A subagent's result arrives on its own as a notice when it finishes; never poll list_agents for it; list_agents lists the agent and stop_agent stops it.
Trust but verify: a child's report says what it intended to do, not what it did - check the diff before relaying success.
A notice is information, not the user speaking: act on it, do not thank or answer it. A message from another agent says in its first line who sent it and how they stand to you.
```

parameters:

- `task` (string, required): First task. State the files, changes and required result. Empty only when resuming without fork: starts no turn and owes no report.
- `name` (string, required): Window and session name. Unique among this caller's children; for toplevel, unique among live agents in the session. Resume an ended child with its existing name.
- `model` (string): Model as provider/model-id[:thinking]. Default: caller’s current model and thinking level. Required if the caller has no model. Bare aliases are refused; see pi --list-models.
- `cwd` (string): Existing working directory. Default: saved session's directory with resume_from, else caller's. Continue requires its recorded directory; fork can copy into another directory.
- `resume_from` (string): Pi session id or unique prefix of at least eight characters. Continuing a live session is refused; fork copies it.
- `toplevel` (boolean): Start an independent peer, with no parent, reports or notices. Depth does not apply. Fork is allowed; an existing child cannot become a peer.
- `fork` (boolean): Copy resume_from, or this session when omitted. A copy requires a task. Defaults to false.
- `runtime` (string): Run the agent's tools in a configured runtime or an ad-hoc runtime of this session by name. Its pi runs here, so resume_from and fork work; a runtime that runs pi itself refuses them. Omitted: the runtime of the caller.

### stop_agent

description:

```
Stop one agent in your scope: a subagent, a peer, an ancestor or a pi the user started. It asks the agent to shut down and then kills its pane. force kills an agent that is not receiving messages. The result is the only signal: a subagent you stop sends no ending notice. Stopping an ancestor ends you with it.
```

promptSnippet:

```
stop_agent(agent, force?) - end one agent in your scope
```

parameters:

- `agent` (string, required): An address: session id, unique id prefix of at least 8 characters, name, or an @-mention such as @impl (session 9702ddd1).
- `force` (boolean): For an agent that is not receiving messages, kill its pane without asking it first. Destructive and irreversible.

### async_bash

description:

```
Run a shell command in the background, for a command whose result you do not need for your next step - this session keeps working while it runs. Exactly one notice arrives when the command ends, carrying its exit status and a tail of its output. Use service=true for a server that keeps running. Its full output is in the log file; read it meanwhile. With stream=true the new lines arrive in batches. list_async_bash lists it and stop_async_bash stops it. If your next step needs the result and you have nothing else to do meanwhile, use bash with a timeout instead.
```

promptSnippet:

```
async_bash(command, name, stream?, service?) - run a command in the background; a notice with its exit status arrives when it ends, read its output log meanwhile; list_async_bash lists it and stop_async_bash stops it
```

promptGuidelines (merged into the system prompt's rules while the tool is registered):

```
Use async_bash when you can do other work while a command runs, when someone (the user, your parent or a child) may need an answer from you meanwhile, when you start several independent jobs at once, or for a server that keeps running. Once a command is in async_bash, its notice is the only way you learn that it ended: never run `sleep` in bash to wait for it, and never loop over its log. If you have nothing else to do, end your turn; the notice wakes you.
Use async_bash instead of background bash jobs (`nohup`, a trailing `&`, `setsid`, `disown`).
list_async_bash lists an async_bash job and stop_async_bash stops it by its job id.
A notice is information, not the user speaking: act on it, do not thank or answer it. A message from another agent says in its first line who sent it and how they stand to you.
```

parameters:

- `command` (string, required): The command to run in the background, as a shell command line (e.g. "make -j8 && ./run"), run through the configured pi shell.
- `name` (string, required): A name for the job; it must be unused by this session's running jobs and children. An ended job releases its name.
- `service` (boolean): A process meant to keep running, such as a server; not a build or a test. Does not hold your report. Off by default.
- `stream` (boolean): Send the command's output to this session in batches while it runs, instead of only at the end. Off by default.

### stop_async_bash

description:

```
Stop one of your async_bash jobs by job id or name. A name selects a running job, or the newest ended job. Its output stays in its log.
```

promptSnippet:

```
stop_async_bash(job) - stop one of your async_bash jobs
```

parameters:

- `job` (string, required): A job id from list_async_bash or its name.

## Messages the extension injects at runtime

Built inside share/pi/ko-pi.ts's closures. `<from>` is the sender's name, else its session id, else its pane, else "another agent".

### a spawned task from the parent (deliverTask)

```
the task text verbatim, as a user message, once
```
delivered as: followUp

### a task from another session (deliverTask)

```
message from @<name> (another agent in this session, not the user):
<text> verbatim
```
delivered as: followUp

### a message from another agent

```
message from @<name> (your parent, who spawned you):
<text> verbatim, as a custom message of type ko-message; the header's relation text by relation:
parent: (your parent, who spawned you):
child: (your subagent):
sibling: (another agent in this session, not the user):
descendant: (a subagent of your subagent):
sibling_descendant: (a subagent of another agent in this session):
the TUI takes the header back off and shows "@<name> says:" with the text, collapsed to its first line until clicked
```
delivered as: followUp

### a message with no calling agent

```
the text verbatim, unlabelled: no agent is the user speaking
```
delivered as: followUp

### a user prompt (ko prompt)

```
the text verbatim, as the user's own message
```
delivered as: followUp

### a steer

```
<from> is redirecting this work: <text>
```
delivered as: steer

### a notice (deliverNotice)

```
notice from <from> (a subagent or background job's report, not the user):
<text> verbatim, as a custom message of type ko-notice; the TUI takes the header back off and shows it collapsed as "@<from> notifies: <first line>"
```
delivered as: steer

### a stream batch (sendStream)

```
job "<name>" output (job <id>)
<the last lines, capped>; when a held line is cut: "... long lines were truncated (the log has them)"; with lines dropped: "... N lines omitted (the log has them)" first; after the budget is spent: "... output budget spent; the log has the rest: <log>"
```
delivered as: steer; starts a turn

### a moved bash call (executeBash)

```
still running after <N> s; it continues as job <id>; a notice arrives when it ends; output so far:
<the output tail>
log: <log>
For ctrl+b or /reload, the prefix is only "still running".
```
delivered as: tool result, not an error

### a cancelled async start (async_bash)

```
could not start background command: start cancelled by session <reason>; no job was started
```
delivered as: tool result, an error

### a replaced registry (adoptJobs)

```
<N> async_bash jobs of the previous ko-pi version were stopped at /reload: <names>
```
delivered as: notice from ko-pi; only when jobs were stopped

### an unknown kind

```
[unrecognised message kind "<kind>" from <from>] <text>
```
delivered as: followUp

### a child's report (handleNotice)

```
notice from <child name> (a subagent or background job's report, not the user):
<its last assistant message's text, then the guidance below>; a report over the 4000-byte notice ends with "\n\nfull report: read_report(\"<child name>\")" before the guidance
```
delivered as: steer

### a child's empty report (agent_settled)

```
subagent "<name>" ended its turn with no message
```
delivered as: the report text

### a turn that ended on an error (agent_settled)

```
subagent stopped on an error: <text>
message it to retry, or stop_agent to end it
```
delivered as: a status notice

### the exit notices (session_shutdown, reason quit)

```
subagent "<name>" is exiting before its first turn ran
subagent "<name>" is exiting without a report on its last work[: its last turn failed: <text>]
```
delivered as: a status notice

### a live job's result suffix for a subagent caller

```
; ending your turn now sends no report to your parent: your report is the last message of a turn that ends when no non-service job of yours is running and no subagent of yours owes you a report
```
delivered as: tool result

### a spawn's result (spawn_agent)

```
spawned <name> (session <pi session id>, window <window id>, pane <pane id>); session id is what resume_from takes later; its result arrives as a notice when it ends a turn with no unfinished work of its own (service jobs do not count) - you know nothing about it until then, so do not report, assume or predict it, continue other work or answer the user meanwhile, and if nothing else is left, end your turn - the notice wakes you; list_agents lists this agent and stop_agent stops it. A fork adds ", forked from session <source session id>" before the semicolon. Toplevel instead ends with "independent peer; no report or ending notice".
```
delivered as: tool result

### a restart's result (message_agent)

```
restarted <name> in pane <pane id>; the same result rule as a spawn follows
```
delivered as: tool result

## Ending notices the extension composes (ko-pi.ts)

`adoptJobs` builds the job notice; `announceEnding` builds the subagent notice when its pane ended or was removed.

```
job "<name>" (<id>) exit <code> | signal <NAME> | failed: <message> | timed out after <N> s
--- last 4000 bytes of its output ---
<the output tail>
log: <log>
```

A stopped job sends no ending notice.

```
subagent "<name>" ended: exit <code> | signal <NAME> | failed: <message> | its pane was removed | its pane is gone; it had reported
subagent "<name>" ended: <how>; it had not reported on its last work
--- last 4000 bytes of its screen ---   [only while the pane lingers]
<the screen>
message it to continue it, or stop_agent to end it
```

Every report notice also ends with:

```


The child stays alive after it reports. End it with stop_agent when you need nothing more from it. To continue it, use message_agent.
```
